title: Gluing multiplicative affine section maps with a common generic formula
statement: Let $p:Y\to Z$ be a morphism of integral schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme] sending the generic point $\eta_Y$ to the generic point $\eta_Z$ [def-sc-generic-point]. Write $K=\mathcal O_{Y,\eta_Y}$ and $L=\mathcal O_{Z,\eta_Z}$ for the function fields [def-sc-function-field, def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Let $F:K\to L$ be a function and let $d\geq1$ be an integer. For every nonempty affine open $U\subseteq Z$, suppose given a map $n_U:\Gamma(p^{-1}U,\mathcal O_Y)\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_Z)$ preserving multiplication and $1$, with $n_U(p^\sharp a)=a^d$ for all $a\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_Z)$. For any nonempty open $V\subseteq Z$, write $\rho_V$ and $\sigma_V$ for the maps taking sections on $V$ and $p^{-1}V$ to their generic germs in $L$ and $K$, respectively. Assume $\rho_U(n_U(b))=F(\sigma_U(b))$ for every such $U$ and $b$. Then there is a unique family of maps $n_V:\Gamma(p^{-1}V,\mathcal O_Y)\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Z)$ on all open subsets $V\subseteq Z$ extending the specified affine maps and commuting with restriction. Each $n_V$ preserves multiplication and $1$, and satisfies $n_V(p^\sharp a)=a^d$. On nonempty opens it also satisfies $\rho_V(n_V(b))=F(\sigma_V(b))$. On the empty open it is the unique map between the one-element section rings. No finiteness or normality hypothesis on $p,Y,Z$, and no assumption that intersections of affine opens are affine, is imposed.

proof.text: For every nonempty open $V\subseteq Z$, $\eta_Z\in V$: otherwise the closed complement containing $\eta_Z$ would contain its closure $Z$ [def-sc-generic-point]. Since $p(\eta_Y)=\eta_Z$, also $\eta_Y\in p^{-1}V$. Thus all the generic germs in the statement are defined. Restricting a section to a smaller nonempty open leaves its generic germ unchanged, by the germ equivalence relation [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. By [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field], applied to the integral scheme $Z$, $\rho_V$ is injective for every such $V$. Consequently sections on $V$ with equal generic germs are equal.

proof.text: If $W\subseteq U$ are nonempty affine opens and $b\in\Gamma(p^{-1}U,\mathcal O_Y)$, the two sections $n_U(b)|_W$ and $n_W(b|_{p^{-1}W})$ have generic germs $F(\sigma_U(b))$ and $F(\sigma_W(b|_{p^{-1}W}))$, respectively. These are equal by restriction invariance of germs from step 1. Injectivity of $\rho_W$ gives $n_U(b)|_W=n_W(b|_{p^{-1}W})$. The same compatibility with an empty smaller open is automatic: the empty-cover sheaf axiom gives a singleton set of sections over the empty open [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0BD3 (divisors-lemma-norm-in-normal-case), proof, compatible affine section maps and hence a global norm map; expanded for the abstract generic formula of this item. Sheaves Tags 006T (sheaves-definition-sheaf), including the empty covering, and 0091 (sheaves-definition-ringed-space).

proof.text: For a nonempty open $V$ and section $b$ on $p^{-1}V$, take the set of all nonempty affine opens $U\subseteq V$, which covers $V$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], and put $c_U=n_U(b|_{p^{-1}U})$. On a nonempty overlap $T=U\cap U\prime$, both $c_U|_T$ and $c_{U\prime}|_T$ have generic germ $F(\sigma_V(b))$ by the assumed formula and restriction invariance. They agree by injectivity of $\rho_T$ [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field]. On an empty overlap they agree because its section ring is a singleton. The sheaf axiom for $\mathcal O_Z$ therefore glues the $c_U$ to a unique section, defining $n_V(b)$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Here $T$ is merely open; it is never assumed affine. Set $n_\emptyset$ to be the unique map of the singleton section sets.

source.place: Tag 0BD3 (divisors-lemma-norm-in-normal-case), proof, compatible affine section maps and hence a global norm map; expanded for the abstract generic formula of this item. proof.text: By construction, for every nonempty affine $U\subseteq V$, $n_V(b)|_U=n_U(b|_{p^{-1}U})$. If $V$ itself is affine, the cover contains $V$, so the new map is exactly the specified $n_V$. For any inclusion $W\subseteq V$ with $W$ nonempty, restrict $n_V(b)|_W$ and $n_W(b|_{p^{-1}W})$ to each nonempty affine $U\subseteq W$. Both restrictions are $n_U(b|_{p^{-1}U})$, so sheaf uniqueness on this affine cover of $W$ gives their equality [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis, def-pc-scheme, def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Inclusions with $W$ empty are automatic. Finally choose one nonempty affine $U\subseteq V$: the generic germ of $n_V(b)$ equals that of its restriction $c_U$, namely $F(\sigma_V(b))$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk].

source.place: Tag 0BD3 (divisors-lemma-norm-in-normal-case), proof, compatible affine section maps and hence a global norm map; expanded for the abstract generic formula of this item. Sheaf uniqueness in Tag 006T and the affine basis Tag 01IT.

proof.text: For sections $b,b\prime$ on $p^{-1}V$, restrict $n_V(bb\prime)$ and $n_V(b)n_V(b\prime)$ to each nonempty affine $U\subseteq V$. Step 4 and multiplicativity of the specified $n_U$ identify both restrictions with $n_U(b|_{p^{-1}U})n_U(b\prime|_{p^{-1}U})$. Sheaf uniqueness gives multiplicativity. The same test gives $n_V(1)=1$. If $a\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Z)$, naturality of the structure-sheaf map $p^\sharp$ [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism] and the given affine scalar identity give $n_V(p^\sharp a)|_U=n_U(p^\sharp(a|_U))=(a|_U)^d=(a^d)|_U$, hence $n_V(p^\sharp a)=a^d$. Every identity is automatic on the empty open. These are sheaf-uniqueness arguments on the affine cover [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis, def-pc-scheme]; no additivity of $n_U$ or algebraic property of $F$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0BD3 (divisors-lemma-norm-in-normal-case), proof, compatible affine section maps and hence a global norm map; expanded for the abstract generic formula of this item. Property (1) of Tag 0BD3; restriction naturality is part of Tag 0091, and sheaf uniqueness is Tag 006T.

proof.text: If $(m_V)_V$ is another extension commuting with restriction, then for every nonempty affine $U\subseteq V$ and every $b$ on $p^{-1}V$, $m_V(b)|_U=m_U(b|_{p^{-1}U})=n_U(b|_{p^{-1}U})=n_V(b)|_U$. The affine opens cover $V$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], so sheaf uniqueness gives $m_V(b)=n_V(b)$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. On the empty open there is only one possible map. This proves uniqueness of the whole family.

It is a one-level split into 6 steps with no new nodes, and its statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to the unsplit node Q92 created. The source is Stacks 0BD3 (divisors.tex 3825-3866): the proof says only 'compatible system of maps on sections over affines and hence a global norm map', and the item supplies exactly that sentence for an abstract generic formula F. The parent normal-integral-finite-sheaf-norm uses it in step 3 with F = N_{K/L}. Checks by step: (1) η_Z lies in every nonempty open by the closed-complement argument, so η_Y lies in p^{-1}V; injectivity comes from clause 1 / the 'in particular' of the Mathlib leaf lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field, which holds for arbitrary nonempty opens. (2) The given affine maps are compatible because their generic germs are equal. (3) Gluing over all nonempty affines U ⊆ V uses the basis leaf, and agreement on non-affine overlaps uses injectivity there, so E1 is avoided. (4) The construction extends the given maps, commutes with restriction and keeps the generic formula. (5) Multiplicativity, preservation of 1, and n(p^♯a) = a^d follow from naturality of p^♯ in def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism plus sheaf uniqueness; additivity is never used. (6) Uniqueness follows from sheaf uniqueness. Edge cases tested: the empty open (zero ring), V affine, a one-point Z, identity p with F = x^d (multiplicative but not additive, so the item rightly claims no ring map), and non-separated Z. Every cited node is a definition or a Mathlib leaf, so the unit route is fine and no tool_uses are needed. proof_deps equals the union of uses, and the searches are recorded, including one LeanSearch outage marked unavailable and rerun the next day.
